title: A bill to authorize the National Library Service for the Blind and Physically Handicapped to provide playback equipment in all formats.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the Senate passed version is repeated here.)

(Sec. 1) This bill authorizes the Library of Congress to purchase, maintain, or replace reproducers for books published either in raised characters, on sound-reproduction recordings, or in any other form (currently limited to reproducers of sound-reproduction recordings) for the use of the blind and for other physically disabled U.S. residents.

summary.headline: This law lets the Library of Congress buy, maintain, and replace playback equipment for books for blind and physically disabled readers in any format, not just sound recordings.
summary.what_it_does: The law allows the Library of Congress to buy, keep in good repair, and replace devices that play back books for people who are blind or have physical disabilities. Before this law, that authority covered only devices for sound recordings. The law expands it to books in raised characters, sound recordings, or any other format.

who_it_affects.group: Blind people and other physically disabled U.S. residents who use the Library of Congress's National Library Service for the Blind and Physically Handicapped
who_it_affects.how: The Library can now supply and maintain playback equipment for more kinds of books, not only sound recordings.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on July 29, 2016.
